title: Wattasid dynasty
capsule: The Wattasids were a Zenata Berber dynasty of Morocco who had served as Marinid viziers before seizing power outright; Muhammad al-Shaykh al-Wattasi formally proclaimed himself sultan in 1472. They held Fez and the northern lowlands but never controlled southern Morocco, where the Saadian sharifs built a rival power base. Repeated Portuguese pressure on Atlantic ports — Assilah fell in 1471, and Ceuta remained Portuguese — weakened Wattasid prestige, and in 1554 the Saadian sultan Muhammad al-Shaykh captured Fez, extinguishing the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Wattasid territorial control is broadly attested in Moroccan chronicles and Portuguese records, but precise border extents fluctuated and are reconstructed from narrative rather than cartographic sources.
